mainTopic: The laws of a mortgaged field (מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא): eating its produce with a deduction or through קיצותא, how local custom decides whose property it is, and when the lender must leave.
overview: This amud opens with the last word of an earlier story: רב אשי treated the orphans as adults. Then רבא בריה דרב יוסף, in the name of רבא, rules that where the borrower may pay back the loan at any time and remove the lender, the lender may eat the field's produce only with a deduction from the loan. A צורבא מדרבנן must use a fixed arrangement called קיצותא instead. רב אחא and רבינא argue whether קיצותא is allowed, and the גמרא gives two versions of what קיצותא means. Even the strictest view allows the סורא mortgage, where the land returns to the owner with nothing owed after a set number of years. Next, local custom decides whether the mortgaged field counts as the lender's property, which affects his creditors, his בכור's double share, and שביעית. The גמרא then discusses harvested dates, a promise by the lender to leave (the הלכה requires a קנין), and how the borrower's words end the lender's right to eat. Finally, some אמוראים refused to eat even with a deduction while רבינא did, and מר זוטרא begins to explain רבינא's view by comparing it to a שדה אחוזה, a comparison that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing word of the previous story: treating the orphans as adults
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the previous discussion: רב אשי treated the orphans as if they were adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...as adults.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes the story from before this section. It tells us how רב אשי treated the orphans: as if they were adults.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because they were treated like adults, רב אשי did not make the lender pay back the value of the produce he ate. Eating it was only a hint of רבית, and a court does not collect for that. With this word the older discussion ends, and a new teaching begins in the next step.

phrases.english: as adults.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּגְדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story about רב אשי from the earlier section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The orphans were treated as adults, so the lender did not have to pay back the value of the produce he ate, since that was only a hint of רבית.

steps.title: Mortgaged field: eat only with a deduction, and a Torah scholar not even that
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרב יוסף, quoting רבא, rules that in a place where the lender can be removed, he may eat the produce only with a deduction from the loan. A צורבא מדרבנן may not eat it even with a deduction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רב יוסף said in the name of רבא: With this mortgaged field, in a place where the lender can be removed, he may eat the produce only with a deduction. A Torah scholar may not eat it even with a deduction.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule starts here, about a lender who holds the borrower's field as security. It says when he may eat the field's produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a place where the borrower can pay at any time and send the lender away, this is just a loan, so free produce would be רבית. The lender must take something off the loan in exchange for the produce. A צורבא מדרבנן must stay far even from what looks like רבית, so for him even this is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: a field given to the lender as security for a loan
where they remove (the lender, once the borrower pays)
a deduction taken off the loan in exchange for the produce

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two levels: the basic rule (eat only with a deduction) and a stricter standard for a צורבא מדרבנן. The rest of the section is about that stricter standard.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rava son of Rav Yosef said in the name of Rava:
This mortgaged field,
in a place where they remove (the lender),
phrases.notes: In this place the custom is that the borrower can pay back the loan whenever he wants and take back his field.

phrases.english: he may eat (the produce) only with a deduction.
And a Torah scholar,
should not eat even with a deduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about mortgaged fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the lender can be removed, he may eat the produce only with a deduction from the loan. A צורבא מדרבנן may not eat it even with a deduction.

steps.title: Then how may the Torah scholar eat the produce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a צורבא מדרבנן may not eat even with a deduction, how may he eat the produce?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then how may he eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the next step. If a deduction is not good enough for a צורבא מדרבנן, what arrangement is?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step only told us what the scholar may not do. Now the גמרא asks for the arrangement that is allowed.

phrases.english: Then in what way may he eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמַאי נֵיכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the צורבא מדרבנן may do, after being told what he may not do.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What arrangement allows a צורבא מדרבנן to eat the produce of a mortgaged field?

steps.title: Answer: with a fixed arrangement (קיצותא)
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the scholar may eat the produce through קיצותא, a fixed arrangement.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a fixed arrangement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the scholar may eat through קיצותא. The details of what קיצותא is come a few steps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So קיצותא is the path that is allowed even for a צורבא מדרבנן. That only works if קיצותא itself is allowed, and the next step questions exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: a fixed arrangement (set terms agreed on ahead of time)

phrases.english: With a fixed arrangement.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקִיצּוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may eat through a קיצותא arrangement.

steps.title: Challenge: what about the opinion that forbids קיצותא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this answer works only for the view that קיצותא is allowed. For the view that forbids it, what can be said?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says a fixed arrangement is allowed. But for the one who says it is forbidden, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. It points out that some hold קיצותא is forbidden, so it cannot be the scholar's way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 assumes קיצותא is allowed. According to the opinion that forbids it, the צורבא מדרבנן would be left with no allowed way to eat the produce. The source for this dispute comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: this works well for the one who says

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
a fixed arrangement is permitted,
but for the one who says a fixed arrangement is forbidden,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קִיצּוּתָא שַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a צורבא מדרבנן may eat the produce through קיצותא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One opinion says קיצותא is forbidden. According to that opinion it cannot be the allowed way out, so the answer does not work for everyone.

steps.title: Source for the dispute: רב אחא and רבינא argue about קיצותא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute: רב אחא and רבינא argue, one allowing קיצותא and one forbidding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: about a fixed arrangement, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says it is permitted, and one says it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting the actual disagreement. It shows that there really is an opinion that forbids קיצותא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 5 depends on there being someone who forbids קיצותא. This quote shows that רב אחא and רבינא disagree about it. We are not told which of them holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught (by the אמוראים)

phrases.english: As it was taught: about a fixed arrangement,
Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.
One says: a fixed arrangement is permitted,
and one says: a fixed arrangement is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִתְּמַר קִיצּוּתָא פְּלִיגָא בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion that the challenge in step 5 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion forbidding קיצותא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The recorded dispute between רב אחא and רבינא.

steps.title: What exactly is קיצותא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the case of קיצותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a fixed arrangement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to define the word it has been using. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand the argument, or why a צורבא מדרבנן could rely on קיצותא, until we know what the arrangement actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? / what does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case of a fixed arrangement?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי קִיצּוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term the dispute is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact terms of a קיצותא arrangement.

steps.title: Definition: five years without a deduction, then everything is counted
steps.stepSummary: קיצותא means the lender says: for up to five years I eat the produce without a deduction, and after that I will count the value of all the produce against the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he says to him: up to five years I will eat it without a deduction; from then on I will value all the produce for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the deal called קיצותא. For the first five years the lender eats for free, and after that every bit of produce is taken off the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the arrangement רב אחא and רבינא argue about. The first five years look like free benefit, which is why one opinion forbids it. After those five years, all the produce counts toward paying off the loan.
steps.confusionAlert: In this first version, קיצותא includes years with NO deduction. Don't mix it up with the second version in the next step, where the first five years DO have a deduction.

phrases.english: Where he (the lender) says to him (the borrower):
Up to five years I will eat it
without a deduction;
from then on
I will value all the produce for you.
phrases.notes: He means he will work out what the produce is worth and take that amount off the loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ עַד חֲמֵשׁ שְׁנִין אָכֵילְנָא לַהּ בְּלָא נַכְיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קיצותא means five years of eating without a deduction, and after that all produce is valued and taken off the loan.

steps.title: Second version: no free eating at all, and קיצותא includes a deduction
steps.stepSummary: Another version says any eating without a deduction is forbidden. In this version, קיצותא means five years of eating WITH a deduction, and after that all the produce is valued against the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: anything without a deduction is forbidden. Rather, what is the case of a fixed arrangement? Where he says to him: up to five years I will eat with a deduction; from then on I will value all the produce for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version (איכא דאמרי) of how to define קיצותא. In this version, eating without any deduction is never allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is in the first five years. In the first version they had no deduction, and here they have a deduction. So in this version, קיצותא never involves eating for free; it only fixes the terms ahead of time.

keyTerms.meaning: some say (a different version of the discussion)

steps.whatToRemember: Basic rule: where the lender can be removed, he eats only with a deduction. A צורבא מדרבנן uses קיצותא instead. In one version קיצותא is five free years and then full valuation. In the other version, free eating is always forbidden, and קיצותא is five years with a deduction and then full valuation. In both versions, רב אחא and רבינא argue whether that kind of קיצותא is allowed.

phrases.english: Some say:
Anything without a deduction is forbidden.
Rather, what is the case of a fixed arrangement?
Where he says to him:
Up to five years I will eat with a deduction;
from then on
I will value all the produce for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי כֹּל בְּלָא נַכְיְיתָא אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the definition in step 8, changing the first five years from no deduction to a deduction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any eating without a deduction is forbidden. קיצותא means five years of eating with a deduction, and after that full valuation of all the produce.

steps.title: Whoever forbids the first version permits the second
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that even the אמורא who forbids קיצותא in the first version would allow the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever forbids the first kind of קיצותא still permits the second kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two versions of קיצותא from Steps 8 and 9. It says the second one is the easier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the lender eats for five years without taking anything off the loan, which looks like interest. In the second version he takes something off the loan every year, so even the strict opinion has no problem with it.

phrases.english: The one who forbids in the first version
phrases.notes: The first version is from Step 8: five years of eating with no deduction.

phrases.english: permits in the second version.
phrases.notes: The second version is from Step 9: five years of eating with a deduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָסַר בְּקַמַּיְיתָא שָׁרֵי בְּבָתְרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two definitions of קיצותא given in Steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second version of קיצותא (eating with a deduction) is allowed even by the opinion that forbids the first version.

steps.title: How can the strictest view allow eating at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: for the opinion that forbids even the second version of קיצותא, how may the צורבא מדרבנן eat the produce of a mortgaged field at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: For the one who forbids even the second version, how is it permitted to eat the produce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. If this opinion forbids even the קיצותא with a deduction, is there any allowed way for the צורבא מדרבנן to eat from the field? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the problem raised in Step 5: what can the forbidding view say? Now that both versions are on the table, the גמרא needs a setup that even the strictest view would allow.

phrases.english: The one who forbids even in the second version,
how is it permitted to eat the produce?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָסַר בְּבָתְרַיְיתָא, הֵיכִי שְׁרֵי לְמֵיכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the strict side of the argument after Step 10 showed which version is easier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there any allowed way for a lender to eat a mortgaged field's produce according to the strictest view?

steps.title: The סורא-style mortgage
steps.stepSummary: Even the strict view allows the kind of mortgage used in סורא: the lender eats for a set number of years, and then the land goes back to the owner with nothing more owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted like the mortgage of סורא, where the document says: when these years are over, this land goes out with no money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The allowed way is the סורא mortgage, where the produce of the fixed years pays off the whole loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סורא mortgage the lender is not getting anything extra on top of his money. The produce of those years simply is the repayment, and then the land returns free. This is a set deal agreed in advance, not interest added on to a loan, so even the strict view allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortgage: a field handed to the lender as security, and he eats its produce
Sura, a city in Babylonia with its own way of writing mortgages

steps.whatToRemember: Even the strictest opinion allows a mortgage set up like the one in סורא, where the produce of a set number of years fully pays off the loan.

phrases.english: It is permitted like the mortgage of Sura,
in which they write this:
At the completion of these years
this land shall go out without money.
phrases.notes: He means the land goes back to the owner, and the borrower owes nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁרֵי כִּי מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא דְסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11, and so resolves the challenge raised in Step 5 about the opinion that forbids קיצותא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סורא-style mortgage, where the land returns with no money owed after a fixed number of years, is allowed even by the strict view.

steps.title: Where the lender can be removed: the land is not his
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע say that where custom lets the borrower pay back and remove the lender at any time, the mortgaged field is not the lender's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both say: with this mortgage, in a place where they remove the lender, his creditor cannot collect from it, his firstborn does not take a double share in it, and שביעית cancels the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement. It explains how a מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא is treated in a place where the lender can be sent away whenever the debt is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the lender can be removed at any time, he never really owns the land. It is only security for a loan. So people the lender owes money to cannot take it, his בכור gets no double share in it, and שביעית cancels the debt like any other unpaid loan.

keyTerms.meaning: They remove (the lender from the field)
A double portion (the firstborn's share of an inheritance)
The seventh year, which cancels debts

steps.confusionAlert: The בעל חוב here is someone the LENDER owes money to. The question is whether that person can grab this field as if it were the lender's property.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
both say:
This mortgage,
in a place where they remove the lender,
phrases.notes: He means: in a place where the borrower can pay back any time and the lender has to leave.

phrases.english: a creditor does not collect from it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל בָּהּ פִּי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: and the firstborn does not take a double portion in it,
and the seventh year cancels it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the legal status of a מַשְׁכַּנְתָּא, depending on local custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the lender can be removed, the mortgaged land is not his: his creditors cannot take it, his בכור gets no double share in it, and שביעית cancels the loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that local custom decides whether a mortgaged field counts as the lender's property, and that changes several separate laws at once.

steps.title: Where the lender cannot be removed: the land counts as his
steps.stepSummary: In a place where custom does not let the borrower remove the lender before the set time, all three rules flip.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where they do not remove him, a creditor collects from it, the firstborn takes a double portion in it, and שביעית does not cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The same אמוראים give the other side. Where the lender stays until the end of the term, the field is treated as his for that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the lender cannot be sent away early, the land is like something he bought for those years. So it counts as his property: his creditors can collect from it, his בכור gets a double share in it, and שביעית does not cancel the debt, because it is treated as already collected.

keyTerms.meaning: A place (meaning: the local custom there)
Where they do not remove (the lender)

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the lender can be removed early decides whether the mortgaged field counts as his property, and three laws depend on that: creditors, the בכור's double share, and שביעית.

phrases.english: And in a place where they do not remove him,
a creditor collects from it,
and the firstborn takes a double portion in it,
and the seventh year does not cancel it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְאַתְרָא דְּלָא מְסַלְּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case of Step 13, from the same statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the lender cannot be removed early, the mortgaged land counts as his: creditors collect from it, his בכור gets a double share, and שביעית does not cancel it.

steps.title: Removal even from dates already on the mats
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא in the name of רב פפא says that where the lender can be removed, he loses even dates he already picked and spread out on mats.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא: with this mortgage, in a place where they remove the lender, they remove him even from the dates on the mats.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains how far the removal goes. Even produce the lender has already harvested and laid out to dry is not yet his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking the dates and spreading them out does not make them the lender's. Once the debt is paid and he is removed, those dates go back to the owner along with the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Mats where harvested dates are spread out

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: And Mar Zutra said in the name of Rav Pappa:
This mortgage, in a place where they remove the lender,
they remove him
even from the dates on the mats.
phrases.notes: These are dates he already picked and laid out on the ground to dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the case of 'a place where they remove' from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the lender can be removed, he loses even harvested dates lying on the mats.

steps.title: Dates lifted into baskets are acquired
steps.stepSummary: If the lender already lifted the dates into baskets, he has acquired them and keeps them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he lifted them into the baskets, he has acquired them.
steps.whatsHappening: The statement continues with a limit. Once the dates are lifted into baskets, they belong to the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting an object is a way of acquiring it. So dates he lifted into baskets are already his, and removing him from the field does not take them back.

keyTerms.meaning: He lifted them (an act that acquires)

phrases.english: But if he lifted them into the baskets,
he has acquired them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַגְבְּהִנְהוּ בְּסִיסָנֵי, קְנָנְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits Step 15: produce that has been lifted is already acquired.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dates the lender lifted into baskets are his, even if he is then removed.

steps.title: For the view that a buyer's vessel acquires, even the mats acquire
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that a buyer's vessel acquires items even in the seller's property, the lender acquires the dates even without lifting them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says a buyer's vessel in the seller's property acquires for the buyer, even if he did not lift them into the baskets, he acquired them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that the answer depends on a known argument about acquiring through one's own vessel. For one opinion, the lender acquires even sooner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that a buyer's container acquires items for him even while it sits on the seller's land. The mats are the lender's own things, so for that opinion the dates became his once they were on his mats. Then he keeps them even without lifting them.
steps.whatToRemember: Where the lender can be removed, he loses even harvested dates on the mats. But dates lifted into baskets are his, and for the opinion that a buyer's vessel acquires, even dates on his mats are his.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says
the buyer's vessel in the seller's domain
phrases.notes: Here the lender is like the buyer, and the borrower's field is like the seller's property.

phrases.english: the buyer acquires,
even if he did not lift them into the baskets, he acquired them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion's result for Steps 15–16, based on the argument about acquiring through one's own vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the view that a buyer's vessel acquires in the seller's domain, the lender acquires the dates once they are on his mats, even without lifting them.

steps.title: Does the lender's promise to leave need a formal act of acquisition?
steps.stepSummary: Where custom removes the מלוה, his condition 'I will not be removed' obviously holds. The גמרא asks about the opposite case: where custom does not remove him, but he said 'I will be removed.' Is a קנין needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that in a place where the lender is removed, if he said 'I will not be removed,' that is what he said and it holds. But in a place where the lender is not removed, if he said 'I will be removed,' what is the law? Must a קנין be done with him, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first sets aside a case that is obvious. Then it asks a real question: when the מלוה gives up a right that local custom gives him, are his words alone enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the מלוה keeps more than custom gives him, and his condition was part of the loan deal, so it obviously holds. In the second case he gives up a right custom gives him, staying until the set time. That is like giving something away, so the גמרא asks whether a formal קנין is needed to make it binding.

keyTerms.meaning: They remove (the מלוה from the field)
I will be removed / I will leave
To make a formal קנין with him

phrases.english: It is obvious: in a place where they remove [the lender],
phrases.notes: This is the custom from step 13, where the לוה may pay back and send the מלוה away at any time.

phrases.english: and he said, 'I will not be removed,'
he did say that he will not be removed, [so it holds].
But in a place where they do not remove [him],
and he said, 'I will be removed,' what is the law?
Must a קנין be done with him, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּאַתְרָא דְּלָא מְסַלְּקִי, וְאָמַר ״מִסְתַּלַּקְנָא״ – מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the two customs from steps 13-14 and asks about a stipulation that goes against the custom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מלוה who promises to leave early, against local custom, is bound by words alone or needs a קנין.

steps.title: רב פפא and רב ששת disagree about the act of acquisition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says no קנין is needed. רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says a קנין is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A קנין does not need to be done with him. רב ששת son of רב אידי said: A קנין needs to be done with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question just asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא holds that the מלוה's words alone bind him to leave when the money is paid. רב ששת בריה דרב אידי holds that his words are not enough, and only a formal קנין makes the promise binding. The next step gives the final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with רב פפא here

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לָא צְרִיךְ לְמִקְנֵא מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: רב פפא said: A קנין does not need to be done with him.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: רב ששת son of רב אידי said:
A קנין needs to be done with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לָא צְרִיךְ לְמִקְנֵא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 with two opposing views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא: words are enough. רב ששת: a קנין is required.

steps.title: The ruling: an act of acquisition is needed
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב ששת: a קנין must be done.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: A קנין needs to be done with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument and rules that a קנין is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where custom lets the מלוה stay until the set time, a bare promise to leave early does not bind him. Only a formal קנין makes him give up that right.
steps.whatToRemember: Where custom keeps the מלוה in the field until the set time, his promise to leave early binds him only with a קנין.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: A קנין needs to be done with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: צְרִיךְ לְמִקְנֵא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute of step 19.

steps.title: Once the borrower says he will get the money, the lender stops eating
steps.stepSummary: If the לוה says 'I will go and bring money,' the מלוה may no longer eat the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'I will go and bring money,' the lender does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new case: what the לוה must say to end the מלוה's right to eat the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even before any money is paid, a clear statement that the לוה is going to get the money ends the מלוה's eating rights. This applies where the מלוה can be removed at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: I will go and bring money

phrases.english: If he said, 'I will go and bring money,'
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the לוה, speaking to the מלוה.

phrases.english: he does not eat [anymore].
phrases.notes: Here 'he' switches to the מלוה, who must stop eating the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: ״אֵיזִיל וְאַיְיתֵי זוּזֵי״ – לָא אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מלוה's stipulation to the לוה's words that end the מלוה's rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The statement 'I will go and bring money' ends the מלוה's right to eat.

steps.title: Argument over 'I will make an effort to bring money'
steps.stepSummary: If the לוה says 'I will go, make an effort, and bring money,' רבינא says the מלוה may still eat, and מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי says he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'I will go and make an effort and bring money,' רבינא said: he eats. מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said: he does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a harder version of the last case, where the לוה's words sound less certain, and two אמוראים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I will make an effort' hints that the לוה may not manage to get the money. רבינא says that uncertainty lets the מלוה keep eating until the money actually arrives. מר זוטרא says it is still a real intent to pay, so the eating stops.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will make an effort / trouble myself
An אמורא who allows the מלוה to keep eating
An אמורא who says the מלוה must stop eating

phrases.english: [If he said,] 'I will go and make an effort and bring money,'
רבינא said: he eats,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי אָמַר: לָא אָכֵיל.
phrases.english: and מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said: he does not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֵיזִיל וְאֶטְרַח וְאַיְיתֵי זוּזֵי״, רָבִינָא אָמַר: אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 21 to a less certain wording and records a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא: the מלוה keeps eating. מר זוטרא: he stops eating.

steps.title: The ruling: the lender stops eating
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא: even with 'I will make an effort,' the מלוה may not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: he does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument against רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any statement showing the לוה plans to repay ends the מלוה's eating rights, even if the wording sounds unsure.
steps.whatToRemember: Once the לוה says he is going to get the money, even 'I will make an effort,' the מלוה must stop eating the produce.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: he does not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: לָא אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute of step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מלוה stops eating once the לוה says he will make an effort to bring the money.

steps.title: How the אמוראים acted with a deduction
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא, רב פפא and רב אשי did not eat משכנתא produce even with a נכייתא. רבינא did eat it with a נכייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא, רב פפא and רב אשי did not eat with a deduction. רבינא ate with a deduction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what different אמוראים actually did about eating produce from a mortgaged field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נכייתא is a deal in which a set amount is taken off the loan each year in exchange for the produce, even though the produce may be worth more. Some אמוראים avoided it because the extra value comes close to ריבית. רבינא held that the deduction removes the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: With a deduction: the value of the produce comes off the loan

steps.confusionAlert: Even with a נכייתא, which lowers the debt, רב כהנא, רב פפא and רב אשי still did not eat. Do not read it as if they only refused when there was no deduction.

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב פָּפָּא וְרַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: רב כהנא, רב פפא and רב אשי
would not eat [the produce] with a deduction.
רבינא would eat with a deduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב פָּפָּא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לָא אָכְלִי בְּנַכְיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the laws of removing the מלוה to how the אמוראים behaved when eating משכנתא produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some אמוראים avoided eating with a נכייתא; רבינא allowed it.

steps.title: מר זוטרא explains the lenient view by comparing it to an ancestral field
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא gives the reason for the one who eats משכנתא produce with a נכייתא. It is just like a שדה אחוזה: even though a lot of produce is eaten, the Torah still sets a fixed amount. The rest of the comparison comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: What is the reason of the one who eats the produce with a fixed deduction? It is just like a שדה אחוזה. With a שדה אחוזה, isn't it true that even though he eats a lot of produce, the Torah says…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings מר זוטרא to explain the reasoning of the one who ate משכנתא produce with a נכייתא, like רבינא in Step 24. He starts a comparison to a שדה אחוזה, and the end of the comparison comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with a נכייתא is that the lender may eat produce worth more than the fixed amount taken off the loan, which looks like extra payment for the loan. מר זוטרא answers with a Torah model: with a שדה אחוזה, the Torah fixes a set price per year even though the field may produce much more. This suggests a fixed, agreed amount is acceptable even if the real produce is worth more.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like; a formula for comparing one case to another
An ancestral field, inherited family land in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. מר זוטרא is only explaining the reasoning of the lenient side, the people who did eat with a נכייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the lenient practice is based on a Torah model, not on a careless ignoring of the concern about extra payment for a loan.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
What is the reason of the one who eats with a deduction?
phrases.notes: He means the lender who eats the produce while taking a fixed amount off the loan each year, like רבינא in the last step.

phrases.english: It is just like an ancestral field.
phrases.notes: The case is a שדה אחוזה that was given to הקדש and then redeemed; see ויקרא 27:16–19.

phrases.english: An ancestral field, is it not so

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא אָכֵיל פֵּירֵי טוּבָא,
phrases.english: that even though he eats a lot of produce,
the Merciful One said

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָכֵיל בְּנַכְיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the lenient practice of רבינא mentioned in Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lenient practice of eating with a נכייתא is modeled on the Torah's fixed redemption price for a שדה אחוזה, which applies even when the field produces a lot. The comparison is completed in the following lines.
